_schema.note: Grounded-advice corpus for the chat coach (CHAT_V2_PLAN.md §3). One card per flaggable (indicator, direction) pair from coaching_scorecard.RULES. get_drills only serves a card when its indicator is CURRENTLY flagged (severity 'review') on the swing being discussed — advice is retrieved, not generated. what_should_change is the measurable prediction the coach verifies on a later session (compare_swings/compare_sessions). direction: 'below' = value flagged under p10, 'above' = over p90. Authored from standard, widely-taught golf instruction; body-posture register per team decision 2026-08-01 (reverses the earlier interpretive-only requirement).

cards.title: Back-to-target turns
cards.fault: The shoulders stop turning early, so the backswing stores less coil than a typical tour swing.
cards.setup: No club. Stand in your address posture with your arms crossed over your chest, hands on opposite shoulders.
cards.movement: Turn your lead shoulder down and under your chin until your back faces the target, hold for two seconds, then return to address.
cards.reps: 10 slow turns before you hit balls; then rehearse the same top position with a club.
cards.feel_cue: Lead shoulder under your chin, shirt buttons pointing away from the target at the top.
cards.caution: Turn as far as your body comfortably allows — a fuller turn should come from rotation, not from bending the lead arm or lifting out of posture.

cards.title: Quiet-hips coil
cards.fault: Shoulders and hips turn together, so there is little separation (coil) between them at the top.
cards.setup: Address posture, club held across your chest with both forearms.
cards.movement: Turn your shoulders to the top while keeping your belt buckle facing the ball as long as is comfortable, so the shoulders out-turn the hips.
cards.reps: 8 slow rehearsals, feeling the stretch across your torso, then 5 easy swings keeping that feel.
cards.feel_cue: Shoulders win the race to the top; the belt buckle lags behind.
cards.caution: The stretch should feel like a gentle wind-up, never a strain in the lower back.

cards.title: Step-and-sync swings
cards.fault: The shoulders out-turn the hips by more than typical tour swings — extra coil that can stress the lower back.
cards.setup: Mid iron, ball on a tee, feet together at address.
cards.movement: As you swing to the top, step your lead foot toward the target and let your hips turn along with your shoulders, so body and arms arrive together.
cards.feel_cue: Hips and shoulders wind up as one piece — no extra twist at the top.
cards.caution: This one is specifically worth doing if the extra separation comes with any lower-back discomfort.

cards.title: Belt-buckle-to-target finish
cards.fault: The hips stall on the way down and stay square at impact, instead of being open like a typical tour swing.
cards.setup: Short iron, easy pace, ball on a tee.
cards.movement: Swing through and keep your lower body turning so your belt buckle faces the target at the finish; let the trail heel release off the ground.
cards.reps: 10 swings at 70% pace, holding the finish for two seconds each time.
cards.feel_cue: Belt buckle beats the club to the target.
cards.caution: Keep the turn level — opening the hips should not mean sliding them toward the target.

cards.title: Wall-seat posture holds
cards.fault: The spine angle changes noticeably between address and impact — standing up out of posture (early extension).
cards.setup: Address posture with your backside lightly touching a wall or bench behind you, no ball.
cards.movement: Make slow swings keeping your backside in contact with the wall from address through impact; the trail glute rolls along the wall as you turn.
cards.reps: 10 slow-motion rehearsals, then 5 half-speed swings trying to recreate the same feel.
cards.feel_cue: Stay seated — chest down over the ball, backside on the wall through the strike.
cards.caution: Keep knee flex soft and athletic; forcing the position rigid defeats the purpose.

cards.title: Doorframe head window
cards.fault: The head drifts sideways off the ball during the backswing more than typical tour swings.
cards.setup: Address posture with the trail side of your head a few centimetres from a doorframe or an alignment stick in the ground.
cards.movement: Make backswings turning your shoulders fully WITHOUT letting your head touch the frame — coil around a steady centre instead of sliding into it.
cards.reps: 10 rehearsal backswings, then hit easy shots keeping the same steady-centre feel.
cards.feel_cue: Turn in a barrel: the head stays inside an imaginary window while the body coils.
cards.caution: A small natural drift is fine — the goal is less slide, not a frozen head.

cards.title: Chin-on-the-shelf swings
cards.fault: The head rises or drops during the swing more than typical tour swings, changing the distance to the ball.
cards.setup: Address a ball with your chin feeling like it rests on an imaginary shelf at its address height.
cards.movement: Make smooth half swings keeping the chin on that shelf — the body turns underneath a level head — gradually building to full swings.
cards.reps: 10 half swings, then 5 three-quarter swings, checking the feel each time.
cards.feel_cue: The world stays level: your eye line neither dips nor rises until after impact.
cards.caution: Level head, soft knees — don't lock the legs to fake stillness.

cards.title: Wide-takeaway towel stretch
cards.fault: The lead arm folds at the top more than typical tour swings, narrowing the swing's arc.
cards.setup: Hold a club normally with a small towel pinched between your lead armpit and chest.
cards.movement: Swing to the top keeping the towel pinned and the hands feeling as FAR from your chest as comfortable — width comes from the shoulder turn, not from reaching.
cards.reps: 8 slow swings to the top, holding two seconds at the widest point.
cards.feel_cue: Push the hands away from your head at the top; the lead arm stays long, not locked.
cards.caution: Long, not rigid — a softly straight lead arm beats a tense one.

cards.title: Bump-then-turn pump
cards.fault: The hips move toward the target less than typical — weight hangs back instead of shifting into the lead side.
cards.setup: Mid iron, address a teed ball with slightly narrowed stance.
cards.movement: From the top, pump the downswing start twice — a small hip bump toward the target that presses pressure into the lead heel — then on the third pump, turn through and hit the shot.
cards.reps: 5 sets of pump-pump-swing at easy pace.
cards.feel_cue: Pressure into the lead heel first, THEN turn — bump before you spin.
cards.caution: The bump is a few centimetres, not a lunge — the head stays back while the hips shift.

cards.title: Post-up on the lead leg
cards.fault: The hips slide toward the target more than typical tour swings — swaying past the ball instead of rotating around the lead side.
cards.setup: Address posture with an alignment stick (or club shaft) in the ground just outside your lead hip.
cards.movement: Swing through WITHOUT the lead hip bumping the stick: the hip turns back and around behind you as you straighten into the lead leg through impact.
cards.reps: 10 easy swings, checking the stick stays untouched.
cards.feel_cue: Lead hip clears back and around, not out toward the target — post up tall on the lead leg.
cards.caution: Some shift toward the target is good — the stick polices the extra slide, not the move itself.

cards.title: One-two-three ... ONE counting
cards.fault: The backswing-to-downswing rhythm is quicker than the roughly 3-to-1 tour norm — the transition rushes.
cards.setup: Any club, easy shots off a tee.
cards.movement: Count 'one-two-three' at an even pace during the backswing, and start down only on the next 'ONE'. Let the count — not the hands — decide when the downswing starts.
cards.reps: 10 shots counting out loud, then 5 keeping the count silently.
cards.feel_cue: Finish the backswing; the ball isn't going anywhere.
cards.caution: Slower transition, same committed strike — don't decelerate through the ball.

cards.title: Compact-top rehearsals
cards.fault: The backswing runs long relative to the downswing — the ratio sits past the roughly 3-to-1 tour norm.
cards.setup: Mid iron, ball on a tee, mirror or phone camera face-on if available.
cards.movement: Rehearse stopping the backswing when the lead shoulder finishes its turn — the club quits drifting at the top — then hit shots from that slightly shorter, snugger top position.
cards.reps: 5 rehearsals to the checkpoint, then 10 easy shots from the compact top.
cards.feel_cue: Turn ends, swing starts — no pause-and-drift at the top.
cards.caution: Shorter top, full shoulder turn — compact should not shrink the body turn itself.
